advancement.create_engines.alive.desc: Get an engine running on its own power.
advancement.create_engines.alternator.de: Turn an Alternator's shaft to put charge back into a Battery.
advancement.create_engines.anti_lag.desc: Set a turbocharger's anti-lag and keep it spooled off the throttle by burning fuel in the exhaust.
Set a Transmission to auto and let it change gear on its own while it is carrying drive.
Use a Bank Builder on a crankshaft to lay out its cylinders and heads in one click.
advancement.create_engines.bank_cams.des: Carry a Camshaft and Cam Lobes when you use a Bank Builder, and it lays the cam line beside the bank too.
advancement.create_engines.big_boost.des: Spool a turbocharger up to a full bar of boost.
advancement.create_engines.blow_off.desc: Dump a turbocharger's boost with a redstone signal.
advancement.create_engines.camshaft.desc: Run an engine whose valves are opened by a Camshaft, geared to half the crank's speed.
advancement.create_engines.charged_batte: Fill a battery with an alternator.
advancement.create_engines.chief_enginee: Finish every track: builder, power, tuning, driveline, fuel and service.
advancement.create_engines.closed_loop.d: Finish the fuel track: burn gasoline, ethanol and waste oil, superheat from the exhaust and light a dual-fuel engine.
advancement.create_engines.combined_cycl: Heat a boiler from an engine's exhaust: set a fluid tank over a hot Exhaust Heat Exchanger and run a Create steam engine off it.
advancement.create_engines.compound_boos: Run two turbochargers on the same cylinders, each making at least 0.2 bar of boost, with all the air going through both so their pressures multiply.
Run an engine at speed cool enough to earn the whole cooling bonus.
Feed coolant, or just water, into an oil pan and let a running engine carry its heat away with it.
advancement.create_engines.coupled_crank: Run an engine of four or more cylinders whose crankshafts are geared together one to one, so they turn as one.
advancement.create_engines.crankshaft.de: Craft a Crankshaft, the spine every engine is built on.
advancement.create_engines.cylinder.desc: Craft a Cylinder, then add a piston and connecting rod.
advancement.create_engines.cylinder_head: Craft a Cylinder Head to seal the bore and hold the injector.
advancement.create_engines.dialed_in.des: Run an engine above 100 RPM with every firing cylinder on a balanced air-fuel mixture.
advancement.create_engines.diesel.desc: Run an engine on Diesel, which lights readily under compression.
advancement.create_engines.dual_fuel.des: Pipe diesel into an oil pan's pilot tank and light gasoline or ethanol in an engine with no spark plug.
advancement.create_engines.dyno_run.desc: Read a running engine's torque and power curves with a Dynamometer set against it.
advancement.create_engines.eight_cylinde: Run an engine with eight firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.encased_shaft: Use Engine Casing on a crankshaft, crank throw, camshaft or cam lobe to cover it, the way andesite casing covers a shaft. A wrench takes the casing off again.
advancement.create_engines.engine_casing: Run an engine with four or more blocks of Engine Casing built round its cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.engine_displa: Point a Display Link at a running engine's crankshaft and show its figures on a Display Board or nixie tubes.
advancement.create_engines.engineer.desc: Burn something on purpose and put the torque to work.
advancement.create_engines.ethanol.desc: Run a spark engine on Ethanol, fermented from crops and distilled in a heated basin. Its autoignition point is so high that boost will not light it early.
advancement.create_engines.ethanol_boost: Run a boosted engine on Ethanol with its charge squeezed past the heat where gasoline would light itself early and lose power. Ethanol waits for the plug, and its boiling cools the charge.
advancement.create_engines.even_firing.d: Run an engine of four or more cylinders whose firings are spaced evenly round the cycle.
advancement.create_engines.every_gear.de: Shift a loaded transmission through all thirteen gears and reverse.
advancement.create_engines.fine_tuner.de: Finish the tuning track: a balanced mixture, MAF trimming and enrichment, a governor holding speed, a fuel tune and a timed engine.
advancement.create_engines.flat_engine.d: Run an engine of four or more cylinders with opposed banks on the same crank throws.
advancement.create_engines.flooded.desc: Crank an engine that sits underwater, or opens its air intake or exhaust outlet there. Nothing burns down there.
advancement.create_engines.flywheel.desc: Run an engine with a flywheel on its crankshaft's line that turns smoothly enough to keep its full rating.
advancement.create_engines.forged_piston: Run an engine with a Forged Piston: lighter and slipperier than a cast one.
advancement.create_engines.fouled_plug.d: Run a spark engine so rich that soot builds up on its plug.
advancement.create_engines.four_cylinder: Run an engine with four firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.full_drivelin: Finish the driveline track: every gear, a charged battery, a flywheel smoothing the engine and a governor under redstone.
advancement.create_engines.gasoline.desc: Run an engine on Gasoline. It will not light by compression, so it needs a spark.
advancement.create_engines.glycerin.desc: Cook plant oil with ethanol and bone meal in a heated basin: you get more diesel than coal would give, and Glycerin on the side.
advancement.create_engines.governed.desc: Let a Governor hold a loaded engine on its setting for ten seconds.
advancement.create_engines.governor.desc: Run an engine with a Governor pulling the fuel rack back to hold it at a set speed.
advancement.create_engines.governor_comm: Power a Governor with redstone so it holds the engine at a share of its setting.
advancement.create_engines.hard_start.de: Start an engine stone cold on ethanol or pressed oil and keep it running until its block has warmed through.
advancement.create_engines.heat_exchange: Run an engine whose exhaust runs through an Exhaust Heat Exchanger hot enough to cook heated basin recipes, with the basin on top of it.
advancement.create_engines.heavy_duty.de: Run an engine rated for 16384 stress units or more: as much as a Create steam engine.
advancement.create_engines.heavy_starter: Get a stone-cold engine going with a Heavy Starter: it chokes the engine into catching.
advancement.create_engines.high_revs.des: Turn a running engine faster than 200 RPM.
advancement.create_engines.intercooler.d: Run a firing engine at 0.3 bar of boost with an Intercooler in its intake, taking the heat out of the air a compressor has squeezed.
advancement.create_engines.maf_enrich.de: Run an engine whose MAF sensor is adding a fifth or more to every shot because the air could burn more than the injector was set to give.
advancement.create_engines.maf_sensor.de: Run an engine with a MAF Sensor in its intake, which sets every shot from the air the cylinder drew in.
advancement.create_engines.maf_trim.desc: Run an engine whose MAF sensor is holding every shot back by a fifth or more to match the air.
advancement.create_engines.mains_power.d: Turn an Alternator's shaft while a cable or machine from another mod draws Forge Energy from it.
advancement.create_engines.master_builde: Finish the builder's track: a twelve with a stiff crank, coupled cranks, a vee, a flat, even firing, a valley cam and a Wankel.
advancement.create_engines.muffler.desc: Run an engine whose exhaust goes through a Muffler: it quiets the note, the bangs and the pops, and costs nothing.
Set an oil pan's Oil Exchange dial and pipe fresh oil in and Used Oil out, so a running engine changes its own oil.
advancement.create_engines.oil_filter.de: Run an engine with an Oil Filter fitted in its oil pan. The oil ages more slowly and fuel is cleaned out of it faster.
advancement.create_engines.oil_kept_fres: Run an engine at speed while an oil exchange keeps the oil nearly new.
advancement.create_engines.overloaded.de: Ask an engine for more torque than it is rated for.
advancement.create_engines.pipework.desc: Run an engine that takes air in and lets exhaust out through piped manifolds.
advancement.create_engines.power_plant.d: Finish the power track: eight steam engines' worth, redline, big boost, twincharging, precision parts, anti-lag and a variable-drive supercharger on its overdrive.
advancement.create_engines.precision_cyl: Run an engine with a Precision Cylinder: a machined liner gives higher compression and less friction.
advancement.create_engines.precision_eng: Run an engine of four or more cylinders built entirely from precision parts.
advancement.create_engines.precision_hea: Run an engine with a Precision Cylinder Head, which breathes better and lights the charge sooner.
advancement.create_engines.precision_inj: Run an engine with a Precision Injector, which atomises fuel finely so it ignites sooner and burns faster.
advancement.create_engines.preheated.des: Start an engine whose block a heat source has already warmed: put a Blaze Burner against its heat exchanger and leave it a while.
advancement.create_engines.pushrod_cam.d: Run an engine whose cam sits beside the cylinder block and works the valves through pushrods.
advancement.create_engines.redline.desc: Turn a running engine faster than 240 RPM, close to the limit Create allows.
advancement.create_engines.reverse.desc: Run a transmission's output backwards in reverse gear.
advancement.create_engines.rotary_engine: Run an engine on an Engine Rotor, which turns on its eccentric at a third of the shaft's speed and has neither valves nor a camshaft. It needs a spark plug.
advancement.create_engines.rotary_revs.d: Turn a running rotary engine faster than 200 RPM, where a rotor keeps its breath.
advancement.create_engines.rotor_housing: Turn a crankshaft with a Rotor Housing in its line: a link that is its own cylinder and head, with ports instead of valves.
advancement.create_engines.service_recor: Finish the service track: an oil pan keeping the oil fresh, a filter, a warm block, an engine running cool, a block heater and a stone-cold start on a slow fuel.
advancement.create_engines.sixteen_cylin: Run an engine with sixteen firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.smoke_signals: Run so rich that fuel pours out of the exhaust as black smoke.
advancement.create_engines.spark_plug.de: Run an engine whose fuel is lit by a Spark Plug, with a Battery to supply the sparks.
advancement.create_engines.stall_recorde: Have a Flight Recorder set against an engine log it stalling.
advancement.create_engines.stampede.desc: Show an engine delivering 500 horsepower or more on a Display Link.
advancement.create_engines.starter.desc: Crank an engine over with a Starter.
Run an engine rated for 65536 stress units or more: four Create steam engines' worth from one crankshaft.
advancement.create_engines.steam_herd.de: Rate an engine for as much stress as eight Create steam engines.
advancement.create_engines.steam_titan.d: Rate an engine for as much stress as sixteen Create steam engines.
advancement.create_engines.stiff_crank.d: Run twelve or more cylinders with no torsional flex: put them on a vee, a flat or cranks geared together, so no crank is longer than eight throws.
advancement.create_engines.sugar_mash.de: Press sugar cane, beetroot or potatoes with water in a basin into Sugar Mash, the start of ethanol.
advancement.create_engines.sump.desc: Run an engine kept oiled from an Oil Sump set against its crankshaft or head.
Read a running engine's Oil Sump with a comparator, to switch a pump or sound an alarm when the oil runs low.
Run a Supercharger at 0.3 bar of boost on a running engine: drive its shaft and put it in the intake run for boost with no lag.
advancement.create_engines.superheat.des: Run a big engine whose exhaust heat exchanger is hot enough to superheat a basin, as a Blaze Burner fed blaze cake would. Superheated, Sugar Mash with a fermenting item and a sugar distils twice the Ethanol.
advancement.create_engines.thinned_oil.d: Run rich for so long that unburned fuel thins the engine oil.
advancement.create_engines.throttle.desc: Run an engine whose intake a Throttle Body is holding partly closed.
advancement.create_engines.timing_tool.d: Use a Timing Tool on an engine to set its throws and cam lobes to the best firing order it can have.
advancement.create_engines.tool_timed.de: Time an engine of four or more cylinders with a Timing Tool so every firing is evenly spaced.
Change gear on a Transmission that is carrying drive.
advancement.create_engines.tuned_up.desc: Sneak-use a Timing Tool until it is in tune mode, then use it on a running engine to set every injector for a balanced mixture.
Spool a Turbocharger up to 0.3 bar of boost. Put it in both the exhaust run and the intake run.
advancement.create_engines.twelve_cylind: Run an engine with twelve firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.twin_rotors.d: Run an engine with two rotors firing on the same shaft.
advancement.create_engines.twin_turbo.de: Run two turbochargers side by side on the same cylinders, each making at least 0.2 bar, so they share the air.
advancement.create_engines.twincharged.d: Run a turbocharger and a supercharger on the same cylinders, each making at least 0.2 bar.
advancement.create_engines.used_oil.desc: Get hold of a bucket of Used Oil. It has to go somewhere: burn it, refine it, coke it into charcoal or let it go.
advancement.create_engines.valley_cam.de: Run an engine where one cam lobe times cylinders on different banks of the same crank throw.
advancement.create_engines.variable_driv: Run a Variable-Drive Supercharger at 0.3 bar of boost on a running engine while its variable drive is overspeeding the rotors, with the shaft well under its design speed.
advancement.create_engines.variable_vane: Run a Variable-Geometry Turbocharger making boost with its vanes partly closed, catching a thin exhaust.
advancement.create_engines.vee_engine.de: Run an engine of four or more cylinders with two banks on the same crank throws, a quarter turn apart.
advancement.create_engines.warmed_up.des: Run an engine until its block has warmed through. A cold engine drags until it has.
advancement.create_engines.waste_oil.des: Run an engine on Used Oil as its main fuel.
create_engines.goggles.alternator.idle: Idle: needs a turning shaft and a battery that isn't full
create_engines.goggles.alternator.no_bat: No battery touching it or its engine to charge
create_engines.goggles.alternator.supply: Supplying Forge Energy from its shaft
create_engines.goggles.battery.flat: Flat: an alternator has to charge it
create_engines.goggles.battery.no_engine: Not touching an engine's crankshaft or cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.broken.hint: A crankshaft has to be one unbroken line of Crankshaft and Crank Throw blocks. Replace the Shaft between them with Crankshaft blocks
create_engines.goggles.cam_ratio.wrong: Must turn at half crank speed
create_engines.goggles.cause.build: A cylinder is missing a part or is not on a crank throw: look at its goggles
create_engines.goggles.cause.cold: The block has not warmed through, so it drags and burns fuel poorly: let it warm up
create_engines.goggles.cause.dry_oil: The bearings are running dry: keep the oil pan full
create_engines.goggles.cause.fouled: Soot on the spark plug from running rich: lean the mixture out until it burns off
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_air: Air cannot get in: an intake is missing, covered or underwater
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_cam: A cam lobe is not opening the valves: touch one to the head and keep the camshaft unbroken
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_exhaust: Burned gas cannot get out: an exhaust is missing, covered or underwater
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_fuel: No fuel is reaching a cylinder: check the injector, the fuel supply and the rack
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_ignition: The charge is not hot enough to light: use a spark plug, a pilot fuel, or more compression
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_plug: A rotor housing needs a spark plug to light its charge
create_engines.goggles.cause.no_spark: The spark plug is not firing: put a charged battery against the engine
create_engines.goggles.cause.too_lean: Too little fuel for the air to burn: raise the injector's metering
create_engines.goggles.cause.too_rich: Too much fuel for the air to burn: lower the metering or let more air in
create_engines.goggles.cause.uneven: The cylinders fire unevenly, so the speed surges: add cylinders, even out the firing order or fit a flywheel
create_engines.goggles.cause.water: Part of the engine is underwater, and nothing burns there: lift its intake, exhaust and block clear of the water
create_engines.goggles.cycle.fouled: Misfire: the plug is fouled with soot and can't light a rich mixture
create_engines.goggles.cycle.no_air: Misfire: no fresh air in the cylinder
create_engines.goggles.cycle.no_spark: Misfire: no spark from the plug
create_engines.goggles.cycle.too_lean: Misfire: mixture too lean for the spark to light
create_engines.goggles.cycle.too_rich: Misfire: mixture too rich for the spark to light
create_engines.goggles.dyno.hint: This is what the engine can be rated for at each speed: after its fuel, mixture, boost and how roughly it runs. Redstone rises as its speed climbs to the speed of its peak power
create_engines.goggles.dyno.no_engine: Not against an engine: set it against a crankshaft, a cylinder or a head
create_engines.goggles.dyno.peak_power: Peak power: %1$s SU (%3$s hp) at %2$s RPM
create_engines.goggles.dyno.peak_torque: Peak torque: %1$s SU per RPM at %2$s RPM
create_engines.goggles.dyno.powerband: Powerband: %1$s to %2$s RPM, within a tenth of peak power
create_engines.goggles.dyno.rated: Rated now: %1$s SU per RPM, %2$s SU (%3$s hp) at this speed
create_engines.goggles.fault.broken_cam: A plain Shaft splits the camshaft: replace it with Camshaft blocks
create_engines.goggles.fault.exhaust_flo: Exhaust outlet is underwater: the gas can't push its way out
create_engines.goggles.fault.intake_bloc: Intake has no open air intake
create_engines.goggles.fault.intake_floo: Air intake is underwater: it draws no air, so nothing can burn
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_battery: Spark plug has no battery touching the engine
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_cam: No cam lobe touching the head or the cylinder
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_plug: No spark plug: the chamber is too long and thin for the charge to light itself
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_rotor: No rotor installed: right-click with an Engine Rotor
create_engines.goggles.fault.not_on_thro: Not mounted on a crank throw
create_engines.goggles.fault.rotary_disa: Rotary engines are switched off in this server's config
create_engines.goggles.fault.submerged: Underwater: nothing burns in an engine that sits in water, wherever its pipes lead
create_engines.goggles.flex: Torsional flex: %1$s%% of the rating lost, %2$s throws on one crankshaft
create_engines.goggles.flex.hint: A long crank twists under load. Past %1$s throws on one unbroken crankshaft it costs rating. A vee or a flat puts two cylinders on a throw, and cranks geared together one to one are separate lines
create_engines.goggles.fouling.hint: Caused by running rich. Lean the injector until the mixture burns clean and the plug cleans itself
create_engines.goggles.governor.commande: Redstone has turned it down: holding %1$s RPM
create_engines.goggles.governor.hint: Fuel (or throttle, in a spark engine) is cut as the engine passes the setting and opened as it falls, over about %1$s%% of the speed. The lowest setting on an engine governs. A redstone signal on the block holds the engine at that share of the setting, 15 being all of it, never below 20 RPM. The redstone output is the rack position, 15 wide open, and reaches comparators only
create_engines.goggles.governor.no_engin: Not touching a crankshaft block or a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.governor.open: Rack wide open: the load is more than the engine can hold at this speed
create_engines.goggles.head: Cylinder Head
create_engines.goggles.head.metering.hin: Too much fuel runs rich and wastes it, too little runs lean. Breathing falls as the engine speeds up
create_engines.goggles.head.no_injector: Right-click with a Fuel Injector to install
create_engines.goggles.head.no_spark_plu: Right-click with a Spark Plug to light fuel by spark instead of compression
create_engines.goggles.head.oil: Takes Engine Oil as well as fuel: it lubricates the whole engine. An Oil Sump does the same without using a face
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.co: Cold: not enough heat to warm a basin
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.di: Heat recovery is switched off in this server's config
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.he: Heating a basin on top of it
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.hi: Set a basin on top of it. About two cylinders at speed heat the basin for heated recipes, about seven superheat it, which doubles the Ethanol a batch of Sugar Mash distils and makes recycled Engine Oil go further. Exchangers on the same exhaust share its heat. The redstone output is how hot it runs, 15 at twice the heat superheating takes
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.su: Superheating a basin on top of it
create_engines.goggles.heat_exchanger.wa: Warm: too little heat to cook anything yet
create_engines.goggles.lobe_shared: Times the first at its angle; the others follow their own crank angles
create_engines.goggles.lubrication.dry: Dry parts drag: pipe Engine Oil into a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.lubrication.thinn: Fuel the air can't burn washes into the oil, however much is supplied. It drags the engine until the mixture burns clean
create_engines.goggles.maf.adding: Adding %1$s%% to each shot to match the air
create_engines.goggles.maf.charge: Air charge: %1$s%% of a full breath
create_engines.goggles.maf.cutting: Cutting each shot by %1$s%% to match the air
create_engines.goggles.maf.hint: Sets each injector's shot from the air its cylinder drew in, trimming a shot that is too big and topping up one that is too small, up to the most the injector can give. Fuel Metering no longer applies. The redstone output is the size of the breath, 15 for one half as large again as the bore
create_engines.goggles.maf.target: Holding the mixture to: %1$s%% of balanced
create_engines.goggles.maf.within: Every shot already matches the air
create_engines.goggles.mixture.suggest: Try about %1$s%% fuel metering at this speed, or tune it with a Timing Tool
create_engines.goggles.muffled: Exhaust muffled: %1$s%% of it runs through a muffler, which only quiets it
create_engines.goggles.oil_condition.hin: Spent oil drags the engine a little. Set an oil pan's Oil Exchange to change it as the engine turns
create_engines.goggles.phase: Top dead centre at crank angle %1$s°
create_engines.goggles.pilot_lit: A pilot shot is lighting the charge
create_engines.goggles.preignition: Charge lights early: %1$s%% of the burn lost
create_engines.goggles.preignition.hint: Boost has heated the charge past what this fuel stands. Cool it with an Intercooler, ease the boost, or burn Ethanol, which waits for the plug
create_engines.goggles.recorder.cause.ov: the load was more than it could pull
create_engines.goggles.recorder.cause.un: and the figures do not say why
create_engines.goggles.recorder.hint: Dots are stalled, light shading cranking, medium coasting, solid running and dark overloaded. Warmth is against the 0.7 a warm engine settles at, so a long way under 100 is a cold engine
create_engines.goggles.recorder.load: Load    %1$s  up to %2$s%% of what it could give
create_engines.goggles.recorder.no_engin: Not against an engine: set it against a crankshaft, a cylinder or a head
create_engines.goggles.recorder.paused: Not against an engine now: the tape is paused
create_engines.goggles.recorder.warmth: Warmth  %1$s  now %2$s%% of a warm engine
create_engines.goggles.roughness: Rough running costs %1$s%% of its rating: a flywheel, more cylinders or an even firing order would smooth it
create_engines.goggles.sensor.no_engine: Not in the intake or exhaust of a running engine's cylinders
create_engines.goggles.starter.idle: Idle: needs a redstone signal and input rotation
create_engines.goggles.starter.warming: Cranking and choking a cold engine
create_engines.goggles.state.broken: Broken: a plain Shaft splits the crankshaft
create_engines.goggles.state.coasting: Coasting: turning, but nothing is firing
create_engines.goggles.state.overloaded: Overloaded: load is more than its rated torque
create_engines.goggles.sump.empty: Empty: fill it with Engine Oil by bucket or pipe
create_engines.goggles.sump.exchange: Oil exchange: %1$s mB of oil a second while the engine turns
create_engines.goggles.sump.exchange.hin: Spent oil leaves as Used Oil from any face, by pipe or bucket, and fresh oil piped in takes its place. Burn the used oil, refine it, coke it or let it go
create_engines.goggles.sump.filter: Oil filter fitted: the oil ages more slowly and fuel is cleaned out of it faster
create_engines.goggles.sump.no_engine: Not touching an engine's crankshaft or cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.sump.no_filter: Right-click with an Oil Filter to fit one
create_engines.goggles.sump.signal: A comparator reads the %1$s tank: 0 when empty, 15 when full
create_engines.goggles.sump.used_full: Used Oil tank full: pipe it away or the exchange stops
create_engines.goggles.supercharger.bypa: Bypass valve bleeding %1$s%% of the boost
create_engines.goggles.supercharger.hint: Boost goes with the shaft speed to the power of one and a quarter, at once and with no need for exhaust: 0.9 bar at 128 RPM, and already 40 percent of that at half the speed. The work of turning it is stress on the shaft, so gear it for the boost you want. Redstone opens the bypass fully. A Variable-Drive Supercharger overspeeds its rotors while the shaft is slow, so it boosts sooner, takes less power to turn and runs cooler
create_engines.goggles.supercharger.no_e: Not on an engine's intake: nothing is boosted
create_engines.goggles.supercharger.over: Variable drive overspeeding the rotors by %1$s%%
create_engines.goggles.temperature.cold: Engine cold: it drags until it has warmed through
create_engines.goggles.temperature.cooli: Cooling down: the metal ticks as it gives up its heat
Running a cold engine drags and burns fuel poorly, and pressed oil and ethanol are the worst at it. Gasoline copes best
create_engines.goggles.temperature.hint: Coolant, or water, piped into an oil pan would cool it, and a cool engine earns a power bonus. A hot engine is never harmed
create_engines.goggles.temperature.prehe: Warmed by a heat source against the exchanger
create_engines.goggles.throttle.hint: Redstone opens it from its idle stop to wide open. Less air means less power, and its linkage trims the injectors' fuel to match. Set the wide-open bore above 100% and a full signal opens it past the plain intake: a fast engine that cannot fill gets more air, which is how it turns faster
create_engines.goggles.transmission.auto: Auto, in gear %1$s: %2$s turns of the input to one of the output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.gear: Gear %1$s: %2$s turns of the input to one of the output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.hint: The panel sets the gear: neutral, thirteen forward gears, reverse, or Auto. Auto takes the tallest gear the engine can pull without overloading, down to a lower one when the load is too heavy and up again when there is room. A redstone signal picks a gear instead: 1 neutral, 2 to 14 first to thirteenth, 15 reverse. A low gear lets the engine carry a heavier load at a slower output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.neut: Neutral: no drive reaches the output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.reve: Reverse: %1$s turns of the input to one of the output, backwards
create_engines.goggles.turbo.anti_lag: Anti-lag: burning fuel in the exhaust to hold the boost
create_engines.goggles.turbo.anti_lag.ar: Anti-lag level %1$s: burns fuel in the exhaust when the engine is off the throttle
create_engines.goggles.turbo.hint: Driven by the heat of the exhaust, so it lags and fades with the fuel. Boost packs in more air, which needs more fuel metering to use, and heats the charge. Redstone opens the wastegate fully. A variable-geometry turbo closes its vanes when the exhaust is thin, so it spools sooner and chokes the exhaust less at full flow. Anti-lag burns fuel ahead of the turbine when the engine is off the throttle, so the boost is waiting when it opens again. Turbos in series on one intake run compound, their pressures multiplying, while turbos side by side (the air can go round either) share the flow and average their pressures, with smaller wheels that spool sooner
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_compress: Compressor is not on an engine's intake: nothing is boosted
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_engine: Not on an engine's intake or exhaust
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_turbine: Turbine is not on an engine's exhaust: nothing drives it
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_1: Every cylinder head needs an intake and an exhaust on its free faces.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_2: Intake Manifolds are pipes. They connect to the heads, pipes and openings beside them, and run from the heads to an Air Intake.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_3: Exhaust Manifolds do the same for an Exhaust Outlet, as pipes can bend and join like a real exhaust. Each opening comfortably serves two cylinders.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_4: A Wrench cuts or restores the pipe connection on the side you click, so two runs can lie side by side without joining.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_5: Openings need a clear mouth. Covering the air intake starves every cylinder on it; an engine that cannot exhaust chokes on its own burned gas.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_6: Smoke from the outlet follows each firing. Black smoke means more fuel than air: the engine is running rich. Turn down the Fuel Metering on its cylinder heads.
create_engines.ponder.bank_builder.text_: Every cylinder wants a block, a head, a piston, a rod and an injector. The Bank Builder places a whole bank in one click.

Use it on a throw: the cylinder and head go on the face you click, on every throw of the crankshaft. It takes blocks, pistons, rods and injectors from your pockets, and spark plugs too if you carry any: a diesel needs none.
Sneak-use changes the layout, and then between standard and precision parts, which it also swaps in for the standard ones on the throws. Flat builds the opposite face too, for a boxer.

Vee builds the face a quarter turn round instead, for a 90 degree V. Carry a Camshaft and Cam Lobes and it lays the cam line too: beside each cylinder block, or in the valley of a vee, where one lobe times both banks. Gear it to half the crank's speed, add pipes and fuel, and let the Timing Tool set the firing order.
create_engines.ponder.black_box.text_1: An engine that stalls rarely says why, and by the time you look it is cold. The Black Box remembers.
create_engines.ponder.black_box.text_2: Set it against any block of a built engine: a crankshaft, a cylinder or a head. Once a second it notes the engine's speed, its load and how warm it is, and keeps the last ten minutes.
create_engines.ponder.black_box.text_3: Goggles on it read the tape back as rows of bars, oldest first, with a mark for each state the engine was in: stalled, cranking, coasting, running or overloaded.
create_engines.ponder.black_box.text_4: Every time the engine changes state it logs the change, and says what the figures point to: no fuel reaching it, a load more than it could pull, or no oil.
create_engines.ponder.black_box.text_5: The tape is kept in the block, so it is still there after the world is saved and loaded.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_1: A Cam Lobe touching a cylinder head, or the cylinder block below it, opens its valves and fires its injector as the camshaft turns. Keep the camshaft unbroken: a plain Shaft between its blocks leaves the lobes cut off from it with no cam.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_2: In a four-stroke engine the camshaft must turn at exactly half crank speed. Gear it from the crank, for example with a small cogwheel driving a large one.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_3: The Lobe Angle, set with the value panel, decides when the valves open compared with the piston. Goggles show if it is on time, early or late.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_4: The camshaft turns at half speed, so a lobe angle counts double. Two angles 180° apart both time the valves, but one fires the cylinder a whole crank turn after the other. That choice is how firing order is set; the next page shows how.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_5: A redstone signal on the camshaft closes the fuel rack. A full-strength signal cuts the fuel and stops the engine.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_1: A V is two banks of cylinders on the same crank throws: here one bank points up and the other north.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_2: Every head needs an intake and an exhaust, and every head shares fuel, so a tight bank soon runs out of free faces for a camshaft as well.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_3: A Cam Lobe works a cylinder from beside its block as well as beside its head, through pushrods. Put the camshaft in the valley, against the cylinder blocks of both banks, and the heads keep every face for pipes.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_4: One lobe works the cylinders on both banks. Its angle times the first of them, and the others follow their own crank angles, so a V needs one camshaft and one lobe to set for each throw. Goggles show when a cylinder is on time.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_5: Add a throw with a cylinder on each side for every two cylinders: six throws make a V12.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_6: It is also how a big engine stays stiff. A long crank twists under load: past eight throws on one crankshaft it costs rating, about 2.5 percent a throw. A V12 has six throws and loses nothing, where a straight twelve has twelve. Cranks geared together one to one count as separate lines.
create_engines.ponder.coupled_cranks.tex: A crankshaft is an engine. A second line of crank blocks beside it is a second engine, however close: each has its own speed and its own firing.
Gear them together one to one and they become one engine, sharing a single set of revs. Any Create gearing does it: cogwheels, chain drives, gearboxes, belts.

Two meshed cogwheels turn the second crank the other way; the engine allows for it. Each throw's angle still sets its own piston's place in the cycle, and the Timing Tool sets the throws and lobes on every line at once.

Fuel, oil, batteries, sensors and every cylinder on either crank belong to the one engine. It is rated and fired as a whole, so wide W, H and X layouts, or more cylinders than one crank can carry, are just more lines.
Only an exact one-to-one ratio couples. Cranks geared two to one, say, stay separate engines feeding one network, and the faster one wins. Goggles show how many crankshafts an engine has.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_1: A crankshaft is an unbroken line of Crankshaft and Crank Throw blocks on one axis. It turns like a Create shaft, but a plain Shaft in the middle splits it and the engine will not run.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_2: Crank Throws carry an offset crank pin. Cylinders mount on any of their four sides.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_3: Each piston reaches the top of its stroke when the crank pin points up its bore.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_4: A throw's angle can be changed with its value panel. Here the second throw is turned 180°, so its piston peaks half a turn after the first. Spreading the throws like this is how firings are spaced out; see Firing Order and Smooth Running.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_5: Cylinders on different faces of one throw share its pin. This makes a V layout: you never pick an engine type, you build it.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_6: One crankshaft is one engine. It drives the kinetic network through the shafts and gears at its ends.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_1: A Cylinder sits on a Crank Throw, its bore pointing away from the crank.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_2: Install a Connecting Rod and an Engine Piston by right-clicking. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to take them out.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_3: A Cylinder Head closes the bore. It holds the valves and a Fuel Injector, which must be installed.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_4: The head's other faces are its connections: an intake and an exhaust. A Cam Lobe touching the head, or the cylinder below it, works the valves and injector.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_5: Fuel is piped into any face of a head. Every head on the crankshaft shares its fuel, so one pipe can feed the whole engine.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_6: Engine Oil goes in the same way, into a second tank beside the fuel. It lubricates every moving part of the engine, not just this cylinder.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_7: Goggles on any engine part show whether that cylinder is firing, and if not, why.
create_engines.ponder.dyno.text_1: How much can this engine carry, and at what speed? The Dynamometer answers.
create_engines.ponder.dyno.text_2: Set it against any crankshaft block, cylinder or head. Goggles on it draw the engine's torque and power at each speed, with the peaks and the powerband.
create_engines.ponder.dyno.text_3: It shows what the engine is rated for: after its fuel, mixture, boost and how roughly it runs. Change a part and watch the curve move.
create_engines.ponder.dyno.text_4: It gives a redstone signal that rises as the engine's speed climbs to the speed of its peak power: a shift light for a transmission.
create_engines.ponder.engine_casing.head: Cladding an Engine
create_engines.ponder.engine_casing.text: A bank of cylinders with its pipework is a lot of loose parts to look at.

Engine Casing is plain riveted plate for building a cowl round an engine. It does nothing to how the engine runs, and it can be used on shafts, cogwheels, cylinders and pipes too. Casing beside casing joins into one plate, so clad it however you like.
Leave the faces that pipes, sensors, the camshaft and an oil sump use clear: casing joins nothing, so it cannot stand in for them.
create_engines.ponder.engine_readouts.te: Goggles show an engine's figures, but only from beside it. A Display Link can carry them anywhere.

Set a Display Link against any crankshaft block of an engine, and give it a display board or nixie tubes. Engine Status lists what the engine is doing, its speed, load, temperature and oil, a line each.

Engine Speed gives the RPM for a nixie tube. Engine Load, Temperature and Oil Condition each give a percentage or a progress bar. Load is how much of its rating the network asks of it, and temperature reads 100 when the block is warm.
Against an oil sump, Oil Sump Levels lists what is in each of its four tanks. A comparator on the sump reads one of them too, to switch a pump or sound an alarm when the oil runs low.
create_engines.ponder.firing_order.text_: A four-stroke cylinder gives one power stroke every two turns of the crank: 720°. The rest of the time it only drags on the crankshaft, so a lone cylinder makes the engine surge with each stroke and slow between them. That surge is the speed ripple.
Goggles on a crankshaft show the firing intervals and the Speed ripple, which turns gold when the engine runs rough. Goggles on a cylinder show the crank angle its piston peaks at.

Mass smooths the rest. A Create Flywheel on the crankshaft's axis adds rotating inertia, so each power stroke changes the speed less and the engine carries through its compression strokes. Even spacing and enough inertia together give a low speed ripple.

To plan one by hand, read each piston's top dead centre angle from goggles. Its firing point in the 720° cycle is that angle, plus 360° if its lobe is on the second turn, and the lobe angle is half the firing point. Choose them so the points fall 720° ÷ cylinders apart. A Timing Tool does all of this for you.

More cylinders only smooth the engine if they fire at different moments. As built, pistons 1 and 4 reach the top together and so do 2 and 3, so all four fire in two bunches 180° apart, then nothing for 540°. The speed ripple stays high.

Two angles set when each cylinder fires. A crank throw's angle sets where in one turn its piston peaks: turn a throw, and its piston peaks that much sooner or later. Throws 2 and 3 here are turned 180°, so their pistons peak half a turn after 1 and 4.

A cam lobe's angle sets which turn. The camshaft runs at half speed, so a lobe angle counts double: a lobe 180° further round times its cylinder just as well, but fires it a whole crank turn later. Cylinders 3 and 4 are moved on to the second turn.

Now they fire one after another in the order 1, 3, 4, 2, a power stroke every 180°. Some cylinder is always pushing, so the speed hardly moves. Aim for 720° ÷ cylinders between firings: 180° for four, 120° for six, 90° for eight.
create_engines.ponder.flywheel.text_1: A power stroke pushes the crank hard, and the strokes between only drag. The speed surges with every cycle, and a Create network wants a steady torque, not pulses.
create_engines.ponder.flywheel.text_2: So a rough engine is rated for less. The more it surges, the more of its torque goes unused: up to two fifths of it. Goggles on the crankshaft show the cost.
create_engines.ponder.flywheel.text_3: A Cast Flywheel on the crankshaft's shaft line is cheap rotating mass. Each stroke then changes the speed less, and the rating comes back. A Create Flywheel does the same, a little heavier.
create_engines.ponder.flywheel.text_4: Cylinders firing evenly smooth an engine too, and a faster engine surges less. Mass costs spin-up and starter effort, so it matters most for small, slow engines.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_1: Seeds or saplings pressed in a Basin make Plant Oil, six seeds to 100 mB or two saplings to 50 mB. Sugar cane, beetroot or potatoes pressed with water make Sugar Mash.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_2: Over a blaze burner, or an Exhaust Heat Exchanger, a heated Basin cooks Plant Oil with coal into Diesel, and Sugar Mash with an apple or any mushroom into Ethanol.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_3: Plant Oil, Ethanol and bone meal make more Diesel, with Glycerin on the side. Plant Oil with Glycerin makes a better Engine Oil.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_4: Heated too, Diesel with blaze powder cracks into Gasoline, at no more than the cost of making Diesel.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_5: Superheated, as over a big engine's Exhaust Heat Exchanger, Sugar Mash with an apple or mushroom and a sugar distils 100 mB of Ethanol instead of 50. Create runs the recipe that asks for the most items, so the extra sugar is what selects it.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_6: Diesel burns by compression alone. Gasoline and Ethanol need a spark plug, or a diesel pilot shot. Ethanol carries less energy than gasoline, but a hot, boosted charge will not light it early.
create_engines.ponder.fuels.text_7: Water with Glycerin makes Engine Coolant. Used Oil from an oil exchange heated with charcoal makes Engine Oil again, 300 mB instead of 250 if superheated with a clay ball as well, or coked on its own it makes charcoal, which goes back into Diesel. Nothing is wasted.
create_engines.ponder.governor.header: Holding an Engine at a Speed
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_1: An engine's speed depends on its load: let go of it and it races, load it and it lugs down. Everything it drives runs at whatever pace that happens to be.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_2: A Governor set against a crankshaft block or a cylinder head moves the fuel rack to hold the crank at a set speed: it eases the fuel off as the engine speeds up and opens it as it slows.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_3: Its Governed Speed is set with the value panel to any exact speed up to 256 RPM, or in steps of 5 up to 1000. A spark engine is governed on its throttle instead, because a charge that is too lean will not light.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_4: It holds the speed with the torque in hand, so the engine's rating is untouched. If the load is more than the engine can carry at that speed, the rack stays wide open and the engine slows.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_5: A comparator reads how far open the rack is held, 15 wide open and 0 shut, so it works as a load meter. The Governor never powers its neighbours directly.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_6: Power the Governor with redstone and it holds only that share of its setting: strength 15 is all of it, 8 about half, never below 20 RPM. A circuit can command an engine's speed.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_7: It also eases the fuel off whenever the engine would race, so an unloaded governed engine idles on a fraction of the fuel a racing one burns.
create_engines.ponder.heat_exchanger.tex: An Exhaust Heat Exchanger is a length of exhaust pipe that takes the heat out of the gas going through it.
A Basin set on top of it reads that heat as if it stood on a blaze burner, so a running engine can cook its own fuel.
From about two cylinders running at speed it counts as heated: enough for the diesel, ethanol and biodiesel recipes.
From about seven it counts as superheated, like a blaze burner fed blaze cake: enough to distil Ethanol twice as far and to recycle Used Oil into more Engine Oil.

It warms and cools over about a second and costs the engine nothing. Its heat also comes out as a redstone signal, and goggles read it in heat per second. The server config can switch heat recovery off.

A fluid tank in its place is a boiler heated the same way: kindled is one level of boiler and seething is two. Put Create steam engines on it, and their power adds to the engine's: a combined cycle, from heat that was going up the chimney.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_1: Crankshaft bearings, pistons and connecting rods all rub against something. They need a film of oil to slide.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_2: A new engine is dry. Dry parts drag: an engine with no oil still runs, but tops out at about half its speed and has less torque to spare.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_3: Pipe Engine Oil into any face of a Cylinder Head. It has a second tank for oil, apart from the fuel. Every head on the crankshaft shares it.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_4: Once oil reaches the engine, the film builds within seconds and friction drops. The engine can turn faster and has more torque to spare.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_5: Turning wears the oil off a little at a time. If the supply runs dry the film thins and the engine slows, so keep the tank topped up.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_6: Goggles on any crankshaft block show how well the engine is lubricated.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_7: Engine Oil is made by heating Plant Oil with a Slime Ball in a Mechanical Mixer over a Blaze Burner.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.header: Matching Fuel to Air with a MAF Sensor
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_1: An injector delivers the shot it was set to, however much air the cylinder breathed. Breathing falls as the engine speeds up, so a shot that suits slow running is rich at speed.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_2: A MAF Sensor is a length of intake pipe that weighs the air each cylinder behind it breathes.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_3: Every injector on its network is given the fuel that air can burn, whichever way that moves the shot: trimmed back as the engine speeds up and the air thins, topped up as it slows. Fuel Metering no longer matters, and the injector can give at most twice its usual shot.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_4: Its Mixture Target, set with the value panel, is how lean or rich it holds the shot: 80% to 125% of balanced.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_5: It also puts the size of the breath out as redstone: 15 for a boosted cylinder half again as full as its bore. Goggles show the air charge and how much fuel is being cut or added.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_1: A Fuel Injector delivers the same shot however much air the cylinder drew in. Fuel Metering sets that shot as a share of the usual one.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_2: Turn the dial on the cylinder head's value panel. Each head has its own.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_3: A cylinder breathes less air the faster it turns, so a setting that is right at one speed is rich above it: fuel wasted, black smoke, less power.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_4: Too little fuel is just as bad. A lean cylinder is weak, and a spark engine cannot light a mixture that is too thin or too rich.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_5: Goggles on a cylinder read its air-fuel mixture. Balanced is the target; 2× rich means twice the fuel the air can burn, and 2× lean means half.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_6: Scale Fuel Metering by the reading. At 2× rich, halve it; at 2× lean, double it. Do it with the engine at the speed and load it will really work at, and check again. Goggles suggest the figure when the mixture is off, and a Timing Tool in tune mode sets every injector for you, at the speed the engine is turning.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_7: Anything that changes the air changes the mixture. A turbocharger packs in more air, so raise the metering to match. A Throttle Body cuts the air and trims the shot with it.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_8: To cut fuel to every injector at once, power the camshaft with redstone. A Throttle Body trims it with the air.
create_engines.ponder.muffler.text_1: Every firing is a bang, and a big engine's exhaust carries a long way.
create_engines.ponder.muffler.text_2: A Muffler set in the exhaust run takes the bark out of it. The engine's exhaust note, its bangs and its pops all come out quieter.
create_engines.ponder.muffler.text_3: It costs the engine nothing: no power and no back-pressure. It changes what you hear and nothing else.
create_engines.ponder.muffler.text_4: It quiets the exhaust that goes through it. On a V with one bank muffled the engine is half as quiet, and a muffler the exhaust can go round does half as much. The exhaust pipes join its two ends.
create_engines.ponder.precision_parts.te: A Precision Cylinder has a machined liner. It squeezes the charge harder and rubs less, so each stroke makes more work for the same fuel.
A Precision Cylinder Head has four valves and a pent roof. It breathes about half as freely again, which matters most at speed, and lights the charge sooner.
Two parts are installed like their ordinary versions: a Forged Piston, which is lighter and drags less, and a Precision Injector, which atomises the fuel so it ignites sooner and burns faster.
Each part helps on its own and they add up. A fully precision engine rates well over half as much again as a crude one, and a turbocharger multiplies that. They are made from Precision Mechanisms.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_1: A Rotor Housing is a link of the crankshaft that is its own cylinder and head. Inside, a triangular rotor rides on the shaft's eccentric and turns at a third of the shaft's speed.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_2: There are no valves and no camshaft. The intake and exhaust are ports in the housing wall, which the rotor opens and shuts as it sweeps past. Pipe it like a cylinder head.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_3: Each of the rotor's three faces is a chamber that goes round all four strokes in three turns of the shaft. One of them fires every turn, as often as two pistons.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_4: Right-click to fit the rotor, a Fuel Injector and a Spark Plug. The long, thin chamber cannot light a charge by squeezing it, so a rotor always needs a plug and a battery.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_5: Housings can be stacked on one shaft, each with its own ports. Set the same way, both fire at the same moment and the engine is lumpy.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_6: The Timing Tool turns each eccentric for you: two rotors half a turn apart, three a third. It sets rotors round any cylinders on the same crankshaft, and leaves the cam lobes to the cylinders.
create_engines.ponder.rotor.text_7: A rotor keeps breathing at speed where a piston chokes, so it likes to rev. It burns more fuel and oil for the power than a piston does.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_1: A Spark Plug installed in a Cylinder Head lights the fuel with a spark, instead of waiting for compression to heat it. Gasoline is too hard to light by compression alone, so it needs one.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_2: Plugs fire from a Battery touching the crankshaft or a cylinder head. Each spark uses a little charge, and a flat battery gives no spark.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_3: A battery makes no charge itself. An Alternator charges the batteries touching it, and those of the engine it touches, while its shaft turns, for a little stress.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_4: On the crank's own shaft line, cranking charges the battery and the running engine keeps it topped up.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_5: Each head's injector is metered by hand. A cylinder breathes less air as it speeds up, so a setting that is right at one speed is rich above it: fuel wasted, black smoke, less power. Too little runs lean.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_6: A spark can only light a mixture that is neither too lean nor too rich. Tune Fuel Metering to the speed the engine runs at, reading each cylinder's mixture through goggles.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_1: A Starter cranks the crankshaft block it faces. It is not connected to the engine's own kinetic network.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_2: Feed it rotation through its back from any source. It cranks the engine at the speed it is turned.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_3: It engages while powered by redstone. Turning a dead engine over takes effort, which appears as stress on the starter's input.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_4: Once the engine fires and runs faster than the starter, a one-way clutch lets go. Remove the signal and it carries on by itself.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_5: A Hand Crank on the crankshaft also works for small engines. Bigger engines need stronger starters.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_1: Engine oil lubricates the whole engine, not one cylinder, so it needs only one place to come in. A head's faces are better spent on intake, exhaust and fuel.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_10: A comparator against the sump reads one tank: 0 when it is empty, 15 when it is full. Scroll the upper dial to pick Engine Oil, Used Oil, Coolant or Pilot Fuel. Use it to switch a pump or sound an alarm when the oil runs low.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_11: A Display Link set against the sump lists the levels of all four tanks on a display board.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_2: An Oil Sump set against any crankshaft block or cylinder head is the engine's oil pan. It holds a litre of oil, and the engine draws on it as it turns.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_3: Fill it by hand with a bucket of Engine Oil. The film builds within seconds and friction drops.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_4: Or pipe oil into any of its faces from a tank. Pipes carry one fluid at a time, so a sump takes the oil line and the head keeps its fuel line.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_5: Cylinder heads still take oil too, and the sump is drawn on first. Goggles on the sump show what is left.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_6: Oil goes off with use, and a spent charge drags a little more. Scroll the dial on the sump to set an Oil Exchange: spent oil is pushed out as Used Oil while fresh oil piped in takes its place.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_7: Used Oil has to be piped away or the exchange stops. Burn it as a poor fuel, refine it back into oil, coke it into charcoal, or let it go. An Oil Filter, fitted by right-click, slows the ageing and cleans fuel out of the oil.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_8: The same sump takes coolant, from any face. Water works; Engine Coolant, made from water and glycerin, works better. It is spent carrying heat away, so no radiator is needed. A cool engine breathes better. A cold one drags until it warms up. Nothing ever overheats or wears out.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_9: It also takes a pilot fuel: pipe diesel into it and a compression engine with no spark plug injects a small pilot shot that lights gasoline or ethanol, a dual-fuel engine.
create_engines.ponder.supercharger.text_: A Supercharger is a blower on a shaft. Intake pipes join the faces round the shaft, so it sits in the intake run, or bolts straight to a head.

It pays in stress on the shaft that turns it, and it makes only as much boost as that shaft's speed allows, so gear the shaft up for a bigger engine. Net of that stress it makes about what a Turbocharger does at the same limit, and a Variable-Drive Supercharger about what a Variable-Geometry Turbocharger does: choose by how the engine is used, not by which is better.
It needs no exhaust and has no lag. Its boost climbs with its shaft speed to the power of one and a quarter: 0.9 bar at 128 RPM, and still 40 percent of that at half the speed.
The price is stress. Turning the blower loads its shaft in proportion to the cylinders it feeds and the boost it makes, so geared from the crank's own shaft line it comes out of the engine's output.
A bypass valve holds the boost at the limit set on its value panel; gear the shaft for the speed you want. Redstone opens the bypass fully and dumps the boost.

A Variable-Drive Supercharger, made from a Supercharger and a Precision Mechanism, overspeeds its rotors while the shaft is slow, so it boosts sooner, takes less power to turn and leaves the air cooler.
Squeezing air heats it, whichever compressor does it. An Intercooler in the run, after the compressors, takes 60 percent of that heat back out.
Cooler air is denser, so the same boost packs in more of it, and a charge that starts cooler is further from lighting before the spark. The core costs about 4 percent of the boost in pressure.

Stages in series compound. When all the air has to pass through two compressors in turn, their pressures multiply, and each turbine in the exhaust adds its back-pressure. Stages side by side, with a branch the air can take round either, share the flow: the cylinders get their average pressure, and the smaller wheels spool sooner.

Pick a Supercharger when the engine cannot wait for exhaust: a cold start, an engine that stalls under load, one held at low speed by a governor or throttle, or a load that swings. Its boost needs no fuel and adds no back-pressure, and it keeps its power at high revs and high boost, where a turbine chokes the exhaust.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_1: A Throttle Body is a length of intake pipe with a valve in it. Close it and every cylinder behind it draws less air.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_2: Its Idle Stop, set with the value panel, is how far open the valve rests with no signal.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_3: Redstone opens it, evenly from the idle stop at no signal to wide open at full strength. A lever, comparator or pedal works like a gas pedal.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_4: A second dial, the Wide-Open Bore, sets how far full signal opens it: 100% is the plain intake, and up to 150% is a bigger bore that lets a fast engine breathe more than the intake alone gives. It does nothing with no signal.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_5: Less air means less power: a throttled engine runs slower and has less torque to spare. Nearly shut, the piston spends more dragging air through the valve than it earns.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_6: Its linkage trims every injector's fuel along with the air, so closing it does not flood the engine. Fuel Metering is still tuned for the speed the engine runs at.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_7: Throttle bodies in one intake line act together: the most closed one governs every cylinder behind it.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_1: Set by hand, every crank throw and every cam lobe is a value to work out. Built like this, the cylinders fire in pairs and the engine is lumpy.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_2: Use a Timing Tool on any block of the engine. It works out the most even firing the layout allows and sets every throw and lobe to it, then tells you the firing order.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_3: Sneak-use it to change what it may set: any throw angle (smooth), quarter turns (cross-plane V8), half turns (flat-plane), or cams only, which leaves the crank as built and just times the lobes.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_4: Some layouts can't fire evenly, such as a 90° V12, and a cam lobe shared by two cylinders can only time one of them. The tool says so, and gets as close as it can.
create_engines.ponder.transmission.text_: A Transmission is a gearbox with selectable gears. Rotation goes in at one end of its shaft and comes out of the other at the speed of the gear it is in.
In first gear the output turns twelve times slower than the input. A load behind it asks the engine for a twelfth of the torque it would direct, so an engine can carry a far heavier load, slowly.
The value panel picks the gear, from first to thirteenth, each about a quarter faster than the one below. Ninth turns the output at a little over two fifths of the input...
...and thirteenth drives it direct. The fastest output, but the load asks the crank for its full torque.
Neutral lets nothing through, so an engine can start with no load on it.
Reverse turns the output slowly the other way.
A redstone signal picks the gear instead of the panel: strength 1 is neutral, 2 to 14 are first to thirteenth, and 15 is reverse. Shifting briefly cuts the output off.

Past reverse on the panel is Auto. The Transmission watches the engine behind it and holds the tallest gear it can pull without overloading: it climbs a gear at a time while there is room, and drops straight to a gear that fits when the load gets too heavy.
create_engines.ponder.troubleshooting_ru: The crankshaft's goggles name the engine Healthy, Running rough or Failing, and under it the one cause most responsible. Fix that first, then look again: the next cause shows up.

Misfires: a spark only lights a mixture that is neither too lean nor too rich. Goggles on the cylinder show its mixture and suggest a metering. A plug caked with soot from running rich misses until it burns clean.

Smoke tells the same story. Black means rich, pale grey means lean, and a blue cast means fuel has thinned the oil. A thick white cloud from a cold engine is only steam, and clears as the block warms.
Surging: cylinders that fire in bunches, or only a few at a time, make the speed ripple and cost rating. Add cylinders, even out the firing order with the Timing Tool, or fit a Flywheel.
Dry bearings squeal and drag, and an oil pan that is empty is the first thing to check. Spent oil drags a little more, and an Oil Filter and an oil exchange keep it fresh.

Overloaded: if the network asks for more than the engine can give at its speed, it slows and eventually stalls. Compare the engine's Load with its Available Torque in goggles, and read its curve on a Dynamometer.

After a stop the block cools: the metal ticks, the head shimmers and an exhaust turbine glows red until it has given up its heat. Goggles call it Cooling down. A hot engine is never harmed, but a restart before it cools is easier.
create_engines.ponder.troubleshooting_st: An engine that will not start is missing one of four things: air, fuel, a spark or something turning it. Look at a Cylinder through Engineer's Goggles first. It says what stopped its last cycle, and the crankshaft says what is wrong with the engine as a whole.
No air: the intake has no open Air Intake on its end, the intake is covered or underwater, or the cylinder has no intake at all. Goggles say "Air cannot get in".
No fuel: the head has no Fuel Injector, the fuel tank or pipe is empty, or a redstone signal on the camshaft has shut the rack. Goggles say "No fuel is reaching a cylinder".
No exhaust: burned gas must have somewhere to go. An Exhaust Outlet that is covered or underwater stops the cylinder as surely as no pipe at all.
No spark: gasoline and ethanol will not light by compression alone. A Spark Plug needs a charged Battery touching the engine. Goggles say "The spark plug is not firing".

Nothing turning it: a dead engine has to be cranked, by a Starter or a Hand Crank on its crankshaft, fast enough for the charge to heat and the cam to open the valves. A pilot shot of diesel stands in for a plug.

Cold: a cold block drags and burns weakly, ethanol and pressed oil worst of all, gasoline best. Give it a little throttle and a minute, or park a Blaze Burner against its Heat Exchanger so it is already warm when it is started.
A missing piston, rod or head, or a cylinder not on a crank throw, takes that cylinder out entirely. Goggles on the cylinder list exactly which part.
create_engines.ponder.turbo_tuning.text_: A Variable-Geometry Turbocharger has a ring of vanes before its turbine. At low revs the exhaust is thin, so the vanes close: the gas speeds up onto the wheel and it spools sooner.
At full flow they open, leaving the exhaust a freer path than a fixed turbine would, so less is lost to back-pressure.

Lift off the throttle and the boost normally dies. With anti-lag set on either turbo, it burns fuel in the exhaust ahead of the turbine while the engine is off the throttle, so the boost is waiting when you open it again.
It costs fuel in proportion to its level, and does nothing on the throttle. Set it from the value box beside the boost limit.

The Variable-Drive Supercharger is the blower's version of this upgrade, from a Precision Mechanism too: it overspeeds its rotors while the shaft is slow, so it boosts sooner, takes less power to turn and runs cooler.
create_engines.ponder.turbocharger.text_: A Turbocharger sits in the exhaust line and the intake line at once. Exhaust spins its turbine, and the compressor on the shaft's other end pushes air into the engine.
A Supercharger is worth the same, for other jobs: boost at once, with no exhaust to wait for. See its page for when to choose one instead.
Exhaust pipes join its turbine face and its sides. Here the head's exhaust blows straight into the turbine, and an Exhaust Outlet carries it away.
Intake pipes join its compressor face and its sides. Air comes in at the front and leaves by a pipe to the head, so every cylinder on that line is boosted.
It runs on the heat of the exhaust, so it spools up a moment after the engine fires and fades if the fuel stops. Goggles show its boost and wheel speed.
More air only helps if there is fuel for it. Turn the head's Fuel Metering up to burn it; left alone, the same shot just runs leaner.
Squeezing air heats it, and the turbine holds the exhaust up, so the cylinders push against back-pressure. Under hard boost a spark engine's gasoline can light before the spark.
Its wastegate vents exhaust round the turbine to hold the boost at the limit set on its value panel.
A redstone signal on the turbocharger opens the wastegate fully and dumps the boost, like a blow-off valve. Lifting off the throttle with boost in the pipe does the same.

Pick a Turbocharger for an engine that runs hard and steady. Its boost is free: nothing loads a shaft, it grows with the engine's own exhaust, and it is strongest in the middle of the rev range. It pays in lag, in back-pressure, and in the fuel it needs to keep spinning.
